question: In round 5's PT_PROF cost-share sweep, what did the combined setting PT_PROF=3 (no shadow walk and no mesh closest-hit) measure?
answer:
PT_PROF=3 (skip shadow walk AND skip mesh closest-hit) measured render_ms_best=0.623 ms, render_ms_avg=1.073 ms, gpu_ms_best=0.458 ms at 512x512 / 64 spp / seed 1, 8 benchmark frames.

How I know: it was the last line of the sweep I ran with the scratch profiling build _prof/ (message #57 issued the loop `for P in 0 1 2 4 8 3` and message #58 returned the results table). The same table gives PT_PROF=0 (full) 45.612/45.352 ms, PT_PROF=1 (no shadow) 44.252/44.051 ms, PT_PROF=2 (no mesh) 4.939/4.773 ms, PT_PROF=4 (no NEE) 43.348/43.171 ms, PT_PROF=8 (glass always-reflect) 35.965/35.764 ms.

That combined setting is the key piece of evidence for round 5's direction: with both BVH walks removed the frame collapses to 0.458 ms of GPU time — the ~0.46 ms residual is everything else (primary-ray setup, per-pixel RNG, NEE math, floor shading, in-kernel tone mapping, accumulation). So the two mesh walks account for ~99% of the frame and the closest-hit walk alone for ~89% (~40 ms of 45.35 ms), which is why every subsequent experiment has targeted BVH traversal rather than host overhead, NEE arithmetic, or the glass branch.
